title: [MultiMesh] Individual instance transforms get corrupted on GPU (enormous scale) with frequent per-instance updates — 4.7.1, Vulkan & D3D12
body:
### Tested versions

Godot version: 4.7.1.stable.mono.official.a13da4feb (Windows 10/11, .NET 8, Forward+)
Renderer: both Vulkan and D3D12 reproduce the issue (rendering_device/driver.windows).


### System information

GPU: NVIDIA GeForce RTX 3060 (recent driver). Note: reproduced identically on two supported rendering device backends, so this is not a driver-specific issue.

### Issue description

With several MultiMeshInstance3D buckets (Transform3D format, use_custom_data = true, instance_count = 2048 each) that are updated per-physics-frame for a small number of active instances (~20–50 writes/frame via SetInstanceTransform / SetInstanceCustomData), randomly (usually within a few minutes) one or more individual instances are rendered on screen with an enormously scaled transform — the whole model appears magnified ~100–200× (screenshots show a complete model at huge scale; animation, texture and orientation are all correct).

Additional symptoms:

The corrupted instance disappears when the camera turns to certain angles (individual-instance culling appears to work on it).
A frame-rate drop occurs while the giant geometry is visible (large triangle rasterization).
Crashes/errors are not present; get_instance_transform() readback stays perfectly correct.
Repro sketch (real project usage, no MRP yet — happy to provide/fill in more)
10 buckets × 2048 instances, ~25 active at a time. Every physics frame, for each active instance: mm.set_instance_transform(local, Transform3D(scale≈0.01, pos, yaw)) + mm.set_instance_custom_data(local, Color(...)); on death, write zero-scale + zero-alpha to hide. No other code touches the buckets (node transforms verified untouched; no shared buffers; no manual get_* writebacks).

What was excluded (full evidence chain — CPU/server side is verifiably clean)
Instance data (RenderingServer storage): write-time checks (validity + scale bounds checked right before every GPU write), release-time readback, reuse-time readback and periodic full readback via get_instance_transform() — all show correct values (scale ≈ 0.01) at all times. The corruption exists only on the GPU buffer, and Godot offers no readback of the uploaded GPU instance buffer.
Texture data: the offset map (EXR → ctex, RGBAH, hdr_compression = R11G11B10F) was scanned texel-by-texel: 0 NaN/Inf, max |value| = 152.4 cm (expected ≤ ~175 cm). The mesh glb (positions/UVs/UV2/index buffers) is also clean.
Shader: clamping the vertex displacement in the shader (clamp(offset, ±250cm)) does not prevent the corruption — so it is not a stray/large offset value being sampled.
Bucket node transforms: no code writes them.
Both Vulkan and D3D12 reproduce it, so it is not a single driver backend issue. The RD layer is shared by both backends.
Workaround that works (verified)
Every ~5 s (300 physics frames), re-write all instances of every bucket (active instances ← CPU mirror values, idle instances ← hidden zero-scale). This forces a full instance-buffer upload and clears the corruption:

After applying this, 10+ consecutive runs (both Vulkan and D3D12) showed zero reproductions (it had previously reproduced within minutes on every run).
This strongly points to the incremental / partial instance-buffer update path (multi-threaded dirty-range upload) occasionally writing wrong instance data (e.g., wrong scale or garbage bytes) into the GPU buffer while the server-side storage stays correct.

Note on existing fix #120230 ("Initialize multimesh buffers to 0", merged 2026-06-18, thus included in 4.7.1): we verified that freshly allocated instance buffers ARE zero-initialized in 4.7.1 (readback shows scale 0 / custom_data 0 on un-written instances). The corruption described here happens after correct data has been written — on the incremental update path — so #120230 does not cover it.

Expected behavior
Per-instance SetInstanceTransform updates must never produce corrupted (enormous-scale) instance data on the GPU buffer — the full re-write workaround should not be necessary.

Suggested next step
Happy to provide screenshots and the minimal reproduction project (C# or GDScript) if needed. Also happy to test a patch on 4.7.x branch if useful.

Additional context: this surfaced in a VAT (vertex-animation-texture) crowd renderer: 10 buckets × 2048 instances, high-frequency per-instance updates, zero per-frame allocations, no other engine features involved.

### Steps to reproduce

1. Create a new Godot 4.7.1 project (Forward+). Create ~10 MultiMeshInstance3D buckets with: transform_format = Transform3D, use_custom_data = true, instance_count = 2048 each, and a simple Mesh (e.g. BoxMesh; no textures needed).
2. Every physics frame update ONLY the active instances (~40 per bucket) via set_instance_transform (scale ≈ 0.01) and set_instance_custom_data (A = 1). Randomly kill some instances by writing zero-scale + alpha 0 (hide), and spawn new ones — keep the per-frame writes busy for several minutes.
3. Run and wait: usually within a few minutes, one or more individual instances are rendered at ~100–200× scale — the whole model is magnified (animation/texture/orientation correct; the artifact disappears when the camera turns; frame-rate drops while the giant geometry is visible).
4. get_instance_transform() readback of the corrupted slot always returns correct values (scale ≈ 0.01) — the corruption exists only on the GPU instance buffer (server-side storage stays correct; no readback of the uploaded GPU buffer is available).
5. Verified workaround: every ~5 s re-write ALL instances (forces full buffer upload) — corruption then stops (10+ runs, both Vulkan and D3D12), pointing to the incremental / partial instance-buffer update path.

### Minimal reproduction project (MRP)

Uploaded: Godot_MRP_multimesh_gpu_corruption_4.7.1.zip (GDScript, no .NET needed).
Run it; corruption appears within a few minutes (keep it running).
Set REWRITE_ALL = true in scripts/main.gd (line 25) to compare with the verified workaround.

[Godot_MRP_multimesh_gpu_corruption_4.7.1.zip](https://github.com/user-attachments/files/31883287/Godot_MRP_multimesh_gpu_corruption_4.7.1.zip)
